correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the rotation subgroup is characteristic and every automorphism is (a,b) with a a unit and b a residue. Pairwise interpolation makes one rotation slope global; two reflection indices are simultaneously interpolable iff their gcd difference with n agrees, by the explicit prime-power unit-congruence lemma and CRT. Mixed pairs always interpolate with an independently chosen b. The Chinese remainder system splits reflection gcd-isometries into prime-power congruence-preserving permutations; the latter are exactly automorphisms of rooted p-ary trees, with p! choices at each of (p^e-1)/(p-1) internal nodes. The n=1,2 exceptions are proven directly. The included checker independently tests every pair for all proposed maps n=3..8 and directly tests group multiplication/locality for n=1..3.

originality.rationale: The exact 2-closure of the natural action Aut(D_{2n}) on all 2n group elements is not stated in the primary works examined. Molnár–Šemrl (2026) supplies the group-level two-point definition for classical matrix groups. Yu–Pan (2019) concerns primitive holomorph permutation actions. Grech–Kisielewicz (2022) concerns abelian permutation groups, while Aut(D_{2n}) is generally nonabelian. Klin–Kovács (2010) already provides broad coverage of the gcd-preserving cyclic block factor; the contribution is specifically the full dihedral mixed-orbit interpolation and uncoupled direct product with the rotation unit group, with exact order and non-globality. Equivalent earlier work on orbital configurations may still imply some or all of the combined result, which remains a priority qualification.
residual_risks: Unsearched earlier orbital coherent-configuration or cyclotomic association-scheme results may imply the whole combined classification.

value.rationale: Two-point local automorphisms of groups are a specific recently motivated problem. This theorem completely identifies when local maps fail to be genuine automorphisms for every ordinary finite dihedral group, gives a full direct-product group structure and exact prime-factor order, and identifies the structural reason (uncoupling of rotations from reflection gcd-distance symmetries). The sharp all-n non-globality statement and index are more informative than an example of a single nonautomorphism. The result intentionally does not claim broad conjectural consequences.
